haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image without pushing and runs unit tests only; nothing is pushed or deployed. A merge to main starts a release run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production both deploy the same image, built once from the merge SHA and pushed to registry.internal/shop-api. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: An integration failure gets one same-commit retry; the run ends if the retry fails. A unit failure ends the run at once and cancels running integration tests.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the image named by previous_tag after rollback succeeds. It is found in SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag, and current_tag is then set to it.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers group members, excluding the merge commit author and PR author when different. No approval within 72 h: run expires, nothing reaches production.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS SSM: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout; the canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Canary is scaled to 0 via canary-off; stable keeps its old image, SSM tags are unchanged, and migrations stay applied.
haiku-low.q8: The older run fails its production ahead check, so it ends as superseded, releases production-deploy, and announces in #deploys.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits holding no lock. If production-deploy lock is busy, it waits, rechecks the window, and returns to waiting if closed.
haiku-low.q10: Canary 5xx ratio over last minute, checked every 15 s for 15 min. Fails above 1%, or no value or query error after minute one.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for how approvers learn a run is waiting. The approval request names the SHA and states when the deploy window next opens.
haiku-low.q12: No automatic rollback: run fails, SSM unwritten, a person decides from SSM or the next run supersedes. Rollback targets previous_tag, not the last good image.

sonnet.q1: A pull request (opened or updated) builds the image without pushing and runs make test-unit (about 4 min, no retry); nothing is pushed or deployed. A merge to main starts a release run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: The one image built at merge, tagged with the SHA and pushed to registry.internal/shop-api. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration failure: one retry of the same commit with no rebuild. The run ends only if the retry fails (or unit tests already failed). Unit failure: no retry; the run ends at once and cancels any running integration tests.
sonnet.q4: The run runs deploy.sh rollback staging, which sets stable's image back to previous_tag and writes current_tag after the rollout succeeds. Staging then runs the previous_tag image, found in SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag (current_tag is rewritten to it). If rollback fails, the run keeps the staging lock and a person checks staging and SSM.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, and not the merge commit author or the PR author. With no approval within 72 hours, or on rejection, the run ends as expired or rejected: nothing goes to production, staging stays on the SHA, and the outcome is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In SSM (AWS Parameter Store): /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes previous_tag, then current_tag, only after a successful rollout. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: deploy.sh canary-off scales the canary to 0 pods. Stable is untouched and still runs the old image. SSM is unchanged because the canary is never recorded. Migrations stay applied, since there is no undo, and are safe because they must work with the previous image.
sonnet.q8: When the older run reaches the production ahead check (after approval, window and production-deploy lock), its SHA is not ahead of production current_tag if the newer run has already shipped. It is then superseded: it releases the lock, ends, and is announced in #deploys. The approval is wasted. If production is still behind, the older run can still deploy (known risk).
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits for the next window start, holding no lock, and no deploy starts outside the window. If another production deploy holds production-deploy: it waits for the lock. After the wait it rechecks the window. If the window has closed, it releases the lock and returns to waiting for the window. Otherwise it does the ahead check and proceeds.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio over the last minute, read from Prometheus with the given query. The run (CI) evaluates it every 15 seconds for 15 minutes, starting when deploy.sh canary exits 0. A failure is any value above 1%, or no value or a query error/timeout after the first minute (fails closed). On failure it runs canary-off, releases the lock and fails the run. There is no retry.
sonnet.q11: CI shows a manual approval job restricted to release-approvers. The request names the SHA being approved and states when the deploy window next opens. CI records who approved and when. NOT STATED how approvers are notified. The document lists whether the approval screen can show the next window time as an open question.
sonnet.q12: It is not rolled back automatically, and the document gives no automatic return to a known image. A person decides from SSM and kubectl: run deploy.sh rollback <env> only if previous_tag is the wanted image, run deploy.sh <env> <tag> on a known-good SHA, or leave it for the next run to supersede. Why: current_tag names the last good image, but rollback goes to previous_tag, the tag before that, so an automatic rollback would not return to the last good image. For staging, a failed deploy releases the lock and the next run's deploy replaces the half-new image.
